tools_helpful.evidence: Namespace rewrite and structural scaffold succeeded; app builds (metrics.builds=true) and runs (metrics.runs=true) with all 3 scenario pages present and visually faithful.

tools_helpful.tool: SKILL.md 'Defensive UI for init-heavy and device-dependent pages'
tools_helpful.evidence: Dev-agent applied the ctor try/catch fallback in every scenario page (e.g. Scenario1_PreviewSettings.xaml.cs:39-53 swaps RootGrid for a TextBlock on construction failure).

tool_limitations.limitation: Only covers init done in the page constructor/Loaded (failure mode = blank frame). It does not cover device init deferred to an async button-click handler, whose failure mode is a dead control + lost status feedback on a page that otherwise renders fine.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Extend the section to cover async event-handler init: broaden the device-init catch beyond UnauthorizedAccessException, and restore control.IsEnabled in a finally.

failed_apis.why_tried: Camera preview/photo/video init on Initialize Camera click
failed_apis.root_cause: On a box without an accessible camera (validation/dev environment), InitializeAsync throws an exception type OTHER than UnauthorizedAccessException (e.g. COMException 0xC00DABE0 'no capture device' / FileNotFoundException). The migrated handler only catches UnauthorizedAccessException, so the throw escapes the async void handler.
failed_apis.fix: Broaden the catch around device init to Exception (or add COMException/FileNotFoundException) and surface a status message; the access-denied path the UWP sample anticipated is only one of several denial paths.

special_apis.special_handling: The physical device is usually absent in the validation environment, and the absent-device exception differs from the access-denied exception. Init must degrade gracefully to a visible status message and re-enable its trigger control, not just handle UnauthorizedAccessException.

errors_encountered.error: Initialize Camera button becomes permanently disabled/greyed with no Status output after click (behavioral regression vs UWP).
errors_encountered.root_cause: InitializeCameraButton_Click sets button.IsEnabled=false, awaits InitializeCameraAsync (which only catches UnauthorizedAccessException), then sets IsEnabled=true. When InitializeAsync throws a different exception type, the re-enable line is skipped and no NotifyUser is called, leaving a dead control and no feedback.
errors_encountered.fix: Use try/finally to always restore IsEnabled; broaden the device-init catch so any init failure produces a status message.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Initialize Camera is behaviorally dead in WinUI (disabled, no Status) while responsive in UWP, in all 3 scenarios.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: n/a (built clean; regression only visible at runtime, not caught by the agent)
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Faithfully copied the UWP pattern of disabling the control around an await without a finally, and catching only UnauthorizedAccessException around device init. On a device-less box the awaited init throws a non-UnauthorizedAccessException, so the control is never re-enabled and no status is shown.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Extending SKILL.md 'Defensive UI' to require try/finally restore of IsEnabled around await and a broadened catch for device-init in interactive handlers.

env_issues.issue: Validation/dev box has no accessible camera; unpackaged WinUI 3 run does not honor the appxmanifest webcam capability the same way UWP does.
env_issues.workaround: Treat device init as expected-to-fail in validation: always degrade to a visible status message and a usable (re-enabled) control.
